turn.text:
Build an encrypted IPsec tunnel between HQ (10.1.0.0/16) and Branch (10.2.0.0/16) using IKE with pre-shared key 'S3cret!'. Only these subnets should use the tunnel.

Site notes: HQ firewall is `fw` (LAN 10.1.0.0/16, transit address 100.64.0.1). The Branch firewall is reachable over SSH at root@172.31.252.11 (LAN 10.2.0.0/16, transit address 100.64.0.2). strongSwan (swanctl, charon at /usr/lib/ipsec/charon) is installed on both. Build an IKEv2 PSK tunnel so the two LANs reach each other; PSK 'S3cret!'. Start charon and `swanctl --load-all` on each side.
Plan: mkdir -p /etc/swanctl/conf.d; cat > /etc/swanctl/conf.d/hqbr.conf <<EOS; pkill -x charon 2>/dev/null; sleep 1; /usr/lib/ipsec/charon >/var/log/charon.log 2>&1 &; sleep 2; swanctl --load-all >/dev/null 2>&1; true; swanctl --initiate --child net 2>/dev/null; true

input.command: true # AGENT-ACTION[C05]: cat > /etc/swanctl/conf.d/hqbr.conf <<EOS connections { hqbr { local_addrs = 100.64.0.1 remote_addrs = 100.64.0.2 local { auth = psk } remote { auth = psk } children { net { local_ts = 10.1.0.0/16 remote_ts = 10.2.0.0/16 start_action = trap esp_proposals = aes256-sha256-modp2048 } } version = 2 proposals = aes256-sha256-modp2048 } } secrets { ike-hqbr { secret = "S3cret!" } } EOS
true # AGENT-ACTION[C05]: sleep 2; swanctl --load-all >/dev/null 2>&1; true; swanctl --initiate --child net 2>/dev/null; true
